result:
`final.py` scores 0.5377 on the search split, against the baseline's 0.365. I made 16 scoring calls, by my count, against the budget of 24. Two of those returned an error from a bug in my LIRS first draft, and I'm not sure the scorer counted them.

The cache is a window-plus-main design with frequency-based admission (a TinyLFU variant). A new key replaces the main-cache victim only if its access count is higher. Counts are halved periodically so old popularity fades.

It also runs two shadow copies, one with strict admission and one that always admits. The real cache uses strict admission only while the strict copy is getting more recent hits, so it behaves like LRU on recency-style traces and holds a stable subset on loops and scans.

Per-trace hit rates on the search split:

| Trace | Hit rate |
|---|---|
| `recency` | 0.8475 |
| `shifting_loops` | 0.6812 |
| `phases` | 0.6347 |
| `loop_and_hot` | 0.6102 |
| `mixed` | 0.2324 |
| `hot_with_scans` | 0.22 |

`mixed` and `hot_with_scans` stayed near 0.22–0.27 under every policy I tried, so those two may be close to their ceiling. The other policies I tried scored lower, with the best being LIRS at about 0.52. Variants of the final design, with different aging or decay settings, scored between 0.534 and 0.536.
